answer: Each identity carries one hash chain, appending work to its previous answer each epoch to reach a summit checkpoint audited by replay. A new identity starts with a 45 credit bond in a karst vault only its key can extend. A missing or copied link breaks the chain, burns the bond, and a ripple audit freezes citing links. The k-th fake needs a bond and chain, so 1,000 fakes lock 45,000 credit and produce 1,000 histories, no bulk discount. Chain rental fails: a rented history carries the owner's key, so the renter's mismatch breaks the chain. An honest agent extends one chain and keeps its bond.
